text:
maria-support: Customer escalated — after they created an interface VPC endpoint to our private API they started seeing intermittent 403s. They say no app changes. Any immediate checks we should run?

customer-jones: We see this from the application logs and curl:
```
$ curl -v https://api.internal.redwood/health
* Connected to api.internal.redwood (10.10.5.12) port 443 (#0)
> GET /health HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.internal.redwood

< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
content-type: application/json

{"error":"forbidden"}
```
Also occasionally TLS handshake fails with timeout.

ashley-network: Quick checklist: which subnets for the endpoint, security groups, endpoint policy, and whether DNS override/private hosted zone association is enabled?

maria-support: Endpoint in subnets 10.0.2.0/24 and 10.0.3.0/24. SG allows outbound 443 and inbound 443 from the VPC. Endpoint policy currently (redacted) contains a Condition that restricts by `aws:SourceVpc` to their VPC id. Snippet: `{"Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow","Principal":"*","Action":"*","Resource":"*","Condition":{"StringEquals":{"aws:SourceVpc":"vpc-0abcd1234"}}}]}`

ryan-eng: That Condition stands out. Remember that when traffic goes through an interface endpoint, the source IP seen by the service can be the VPCE ENI addresses, not the original client IP, depending on routing/NAT. If the endpoint policy is checking SourceVpc it might not match how AWS sets the attributes. Also check if the endpoint targets an NLB in our account vs cross-account.

ashley-network: Confirmed their DNS override maps `api.internal.redwood` -> `vpce-12345-abcdef.elb.amazonaws.com`. The VPCE is associated with a hosted zone. Route tables look fine but note: customer used a cross-account NLB target. That can change the source IP seen by the backend.

maria-support: We captured a quick tcpdump at the backend ENI: `13:45:12.123 IP 10.20.3.54.34567 > 10.30.4.10.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240` then the next packet is an RST from 10.30.4.10 shortly after the TLS ClientHello. So connection is accepted then closed.

ryan-eng: Two likely causes: 1) endpoint policy or network ACL/SG dropping/transforming traffic so our auth layer rejects it; 2) SNI/Host header mismatch because PrivateLink DNS points at vpce DNS name and the endpoint may terminate TLS or proxy with different SNI — our frontend may rely on SNI/Host for certificate selection or routing. Do we terminate TLS at their NLB or pass through?

ashley-network: The endpoint is fronting an NLB which does TLS passthrough, but because it's cross-account the source IP visible to us becomes the NLB's IPs or VPCE ENI IPs. Their endpoint policy denies when aws:SourceVpc != vpc-0abcd1234, so our auth (which whitelists their VPC) returns 403. Essentially the endpoint policy is preventing the expected principal attributes.

maria-support: Repro steps we used: 1) create interface endpoint to `com.redwood.api-private` from test account 2) associate private hosted zone so `api.internal.redwood` resolves to the VPCE DNS name 3) curl -> 403 4) remove/loosen endpoint policy -> curl -> 200. So changing the endpoint policy immediately fixed the 403.

ryan-eng: Recommendation for fix: have endpoint policy allow the actions for the VPCE principal or remove the strict SourceVpc Condition. Short-term workaround for customer: update endpoint policy to `{"Effect":"Allow","Principal":"*","Action":"execute-api:*","Resource":"*"}` scoped to the service, or update our auth to trust X-Forwarded-For / mTLS so client identity does not depend on source IP. Long-term: add a KB describing PrivateLink caveats: source IP substitution, cross-account NLB behavior, and DNS/SNI implications.

maria-support: Customer applied a policy change to allow the VPCE principal and confirmed requests returned 200 consistently. They also agreed to a doc showing we recommend header-based auth or mTLS when using PrivateLink. :tada:

ashley-network: Added notes to the ticket about checking SGs, NACLs, and endpoint policy when customers report post-PrivateLink 403s.

maria-support: I'll save the repro and the policy snippet to /kb/private-link-troubleshooting and close the escalation. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Incident INC-12345 closed by maria-support at 3498765600
